headline: A 2014 law requires Medicare post-acute care providers to report standardized patient data so providers can share records and Medicare can compare their performance.
what_it_does: The law directs the Department of Health and Human Services to collect standardized patient assessment, quality, and resource-use data from post-acute care providers. It requires that this data be standardized and exchangeable so providers can share patient histories and coordinate care, including at discharge. It also requires hospice surveys at least every 36 months, changes how hospice payment caps are updated, and creates a Medicare Improvement Fund for future program improvements.

who_it_affects.how: They must report quality, resource-use, and standardized patient assessment data on a three-phase schedule.

who_it_affects.how: Limits on beneficiary liability for denied payments now follow the same rules that apply to other services judged not reasonable or necessary.
Their providers will share standardized records intended to support coordinated care, and public reports will show provider performance.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted October 6, 2014. The summary describes a three-phase reporting schedule and funding periods running through FY2025, but it does not give exact start dates for each provision.
